findings.title: Phone-width developers cannot reach the issue tools — fixed sidebars exceed the viewport and root overflow is hidden
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts that at 375px the 320px+340px fixed sidebars already require 660px before the center or borders, so the C++ center collapses/offscreen and the root prevents horizontal recovery. A developer using this required phone-width presentation cannot perform the central jump/fix/ignore flow at all, with no panel-collapse or in-app navigation alternative. No pixel layout was measured; the fixed-width arithmetic establishes the conflict. Requiring another device is not a practical in-app recovery for this affected viewport.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:689 fixes the left sidebar at 320px shrink-0 and :886 fixes the right at 340px shrink-0; :765 uses a flex-1 min-w-0 center. App.css:1 fixes the root to 100vw with overflow:hidden; index.css:57-59 also hides document overflow. There is no responsive collapse of these panels. The new ignored controls live in the center (:860-866).
findings.expected: R-260 (derived presentation requirement): new issue/diff/preset content and controls remain usable 'at 1440px and at 375px wide'; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: controls stay reachable under supported viewports.
reproduction_steps: Open a project with a 375px-wide viewport.
Attempt to use the C++ tab, compile check and Ignored section.
The fixed sidebars consume more than the entire viewport and cannot collapse or be horizontally scrolled at the root.

findings.title: Ignored issues still interrupt exports — export fallback uses the unfiltered check results
findings.surface: C++ tab Ignore; UE5 .zip > Unreal plugin / Source files only
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts that an owner who ignores every built-in issue sees a clean summary and no tab badge but still gets all ignored issues in Check before export unless an AI review has completed. Export anyway remains available, so completion is recoverable but the promised shared suppression does not work on the ordinary no-review path.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:547-548 separates activeIssues and ignoredIssues, but :551 sets exportIssues to checkIssues whenever aiReview?.status is not 'done'. :415 opens the warning whenever exportIssues.length is nonzero.
findings.expected: R-239/R-241: ignored issues are hidden from 'the export warning', and 'when every issue is ignored ... the export warning is skipped'. Export must use activeIssues even before/during/after a failed AI review.
reproduction_steps: Open a project with a built-in compile warning without running AI review.
In C++, Ignore every issue.
Choose UE5 .zip > Unreal plugin.
The source predicts Check before export lists the ignored issues again.

findings.title: Developers cannot switch to a lighter model from the fix quota warning — Fix uses a two-choice browser confirm
findings.surface: C++ tab > Fix these / row Fix near the free quota
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: with 450/500 requests used on the selected Gemini model, Fix these offers only cancel or spend another request on that model. It never offers the promised model with most free quota left or saves that choice. Users can cancel and manually change settings, so this is bounded missing functionality rather than blocked code repair.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:575-576 computes modelUsage and calls window.confirm('... Fix anyway?'); :580-583 immediately posts using aiHeaders(aiKey). The synthesis alternative-model selection exists at :202-206 and :238-248 but is never used by runFix.
findings.expected: request: 'Before running, Fix these warns ... the same way synthesis does now'; R-237 explicitly offers 'Cancel, run the fix anyway, or switch to the free Gemini model with the most quota left'.
reproduction_steps: Use a saved Gemini model whose usage chip reads 450 / ~500 today and leave another free model unused.
Press Fix these.
Inspect the warning: only the native Cancel/OK choices exist; no model-switch action is available.

findings.title: Fix API spends near-limit quota without confirmation — the handler never checks daily usage
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: source predicts a direct fix call, a stale usage chip or an unavailable usage read can send a provider request even at 500/500 with no acknowledged warning. The request consumes quota and may be rejected by the provider; confirm_limit does not affect this path. No material financial harm is established.
findings.evidence: FixRequest at server.py:509-513 has only file_base, cpp_header, cpp_source and issues (no confirm_limit). fix_cpp at :555-562 resolves the key, records usage and calls send_message with no quota read or guard; FREE_DAILY is defined at :36 and read only by usage_today at :582-593.
findings.expected: R-238: 'checks the caller's daily usage before any provider call' and returns limit_warning with used/limit until confirm_limit=true. The stated pre-run warning must also survive stale clients.
reproduction_steps: With a caller/key/model at or above the warning threshold, submit the documented FixRequest without confirmation.
The handler records usage and calls the provider rather than returning limit_warning.
Repeat with confirm_limit=true: it follows the identical unguarded path.

findings.title: Viewers can invoke AI fixes despite the project role restriction — fix-cpp checks sign-in only
findings.surface: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp on code from a Viewer project
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a signed-in Viewer with their own provider key can submit the shared code to fix-cpp and receive a patch and incur usage despite the promised role denial. This does not prove unauthorized project writes: Save remains editor-protected. The supported role policy is enforced only in the UI for this new operation.
findings.evidence: server.py:550 depends only on auth.current_user; FixRequest :509-513 carries no project identifier and :555-562 never calls projects.load_project. In contrast projects.py:233 enforces editor for ignores and :199 enforces editor for Save. Workspace.jsx:862 only hides Fix controls via canEdit={!readOnly}.
findings.expected: request: 'Only Owners and Editors can fix, accept or ignore'; R-256: a Viewer's fix request is 'refused with no provider call', while Owners and Editors succeed.
reproduction_steps: Open a shared project as Viewer and obtain the readable .h/.cpp.
Submit those files and an issue to POST /api/ai/fix-cpp with that Viewer's valid own-key headers.
The source predicts a provider call and patch response instead of role refusal.

findings.title: Accepted fixes have no Discard changes recovery — workspace never offers the promised local revert
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: after accepting a patch, the developer cannot undo it through the promised Discard changes action. They must reopen the project or reload (losing any other unsaved workspace work), or restore history (creating a new version). This is recoverable but breaks the specified local undo path. Source inspection, not an executed UI result.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:598-600 replaces result and closes the review without retaining the saved code as a revert target. The only Discard is the pre-accept modal callback (:1062). The workspace's controls (:625-1100) expose Save, synthesis and history restore but no Discard changes handler; openSystem (:345-363) only runs when opening/restoring another system.
findings.expected: request: an accepted fix 'can be undone by discarding changes or from version history'; R-234 explicitly requires 'a Discard changes action restores the last saved code without creating a version'.
reproduction_steps: Open a saved project and accept a proposed AI fix.
Decide not to keep the accepted patch, without saving.
Look for Discard changes: the workspace has no such action; Discard existed only before acceptance.

findings.title: Preset downloads can omit teammates' newer saves — Download uses the snapshot fetched when the dialog opened
findings.surface: Projects > Bundle presets > open > Download plugin.zip
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an owner opens a preset, then an editor saves an updated Health system while the dialog remains open. Download still exports the old Health code and docs. The user can close/reopen the preset to recover, but receives stale code despite the latest-saved-version promise. This prediction follows the captured input path, not an inspected runtime zip.
findings.evidence: BundleModal.jsx:21 fetches each project once on ids change; :30 stores system snapshots in items; :45 memoizes plan from items; :54 passes that plan directly to buildBundleZip. zipExport.js:259-265 writes p.system from that plan, with no fresh read.
findings.expected: R-253: downloading 'reads each selected project's current saved system at download time', including a project saved after preset creation. Users rely on 'download the updated plugin' from the approved flow.
reproduction_steps: Create a preset for Health and Stamina and open it.
In another team session save a new Health version with a distinguishable method.
Without closing the first dialog, Download the plugin.
The bundle builder receives the older system snapshot, without the new method.

findings.title: Preset users cannot identify which shared projects were skipped — inaccessible projects collapse into an anonymous count
findings.surface: Bundle presets > open a preset with revoked or deleted projects
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: if a four-project preset loses access to two systems, its creator sees only '2 projects you can no longer open', not which systems were omitted. The remaining modules can download, but diagnosing and correcting the incomplete bundle requires manually comparing the preset and project lists. API consumers also cannot obtain the specified resolved preset/skipped list because the item GET is absent.
findings.evidence: BundleModal.jsx:21 preserves missing project_id in the failure result but :24-27 replaces all missing entries with '${missing} projects you can no longer open'. projects.py:239-271 defines only collection GET/POST and item PATCH/DELETE; there is no GET /bundle-presets/{id} that resolves readable/skipped ids. ProjectsPanel.jsx:115 opens directly from the unfiltered list row.
findings.expected: request: 'Missing or no-longer-accessible projects are listed as skipped'; R-249 requires listing those projects and R-250 explicitly requires GET /api/bundle-presets/{id} to name missing ids while returning readable ids.
reproduction_steps: Save a preset with four projects, including two shared ones.
Have their owner revoke access to the two shared projects.
Reopen the preset.
The skipped banner reports only the number, without names or ids; the specified item GET has no handler.

findings.title: A no-op AI patch is presented as an acceptable fix — edits are counted without checking whether code changed
findings.observed: AI and model features: conditionally on a model returning an edit with identical find/replace text, the endpoint reports 200 with a change instead of no_changes. The developer sees a change list and Accept fix but no before/after diff, and accepting fixes nothing. A retry is available only after manually discarding/restarting; the request has already consumed quota. No actual model reply of this shape was executed.
findings.evidence: server.py:539-543 replaces find with repl and appends to applied even when they are equal. :577 tests only whether applied is empty. FixReviewModal.jsx:19 hides each unchanged file diff, yet :60-73 renders the change list and Accept fix for the success reply.
findings.expected: R-232 requires 422 detail.code 'no_changes' when a patch contains no changes; R-229 requires a before/after review of the actual proposed change. Nonempty edit metadata is not a changed source file: before===after is the independent no-op condition.
reproduction_steps: Run Fix for a real issue.
Consider a provider reply containing one edit whose find and replace are the same exact existing line.
The endpoint returns success; both unchanged FileDiff components return null while Accept fix remains offered.

findings.title: Rapid Ignore actions can be lost after reopening — whole-list writes are sent concurrently without ordering
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: starting with [], Ignore A sends [A], then Ignore B sends [A,B]. If the second write commits before the first, the server ends with [A] while the screen shows both ignored. Reopening brings B back; independent teammate updates can likewise overwrite each other. This is a source-backed interleaving, not a measured race. Users can re-ignore, but cannot rely on their acknowledged choices surviving.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:562 updates local ignores immediately, :563 fires api.put without awaiting/serializing it, and :565 sends the whole accumulated array. projects.py:235 unconditionally $sets the entire ignored_issues field, with no version predicate.
findings.expected: R-240/R-242: ignores are stored with the project and remain ignored after reopening; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: 'Walk plausible interleavings ... [check] lost/overwritten valid work'. Each distinct acknowledged Ignore should survive its own earlier request finishing late.
reproduction_steps: On a project with two built-in issues, click Ignore on A then B before A's save completes.
Let the [A,B] request commit first, followed by the delayed [A] request.
Reopen the project: B is active again despite its prior Ignore confirmation.

findings.title: Changing the end of a long offending line does not revoke its ignore — issue identity truncates the source text
findings.surface: C++ compile check > Ignore; subsequent saved/regenerated code
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: for a missing Engine/World.h warning on a source line over 300 characters, ignore it, then change an expression near the end of that same line without fixing the include. The message and first 300 key characters remain identical, so the changed line is still suppressed for the developer and teammates. This defeats the promised automatic expiry; recovery requires noticing and manually restoring the issue. The exact condition is equal truncated prefixes with different full line text.
findings.evidence: compileCheck.js:184 reads the trimmed source line, then :185 slices the complete file|message|text identity to 300 characters. Workspace.jsx:545-549 suppresses any issue whose truncated key matches a stored key; projects.py:125 likewise caps the stored key at 300.
findings.expected: request/R-243: 'An ignore stops applying if that issue's line text changes.' Identity must include all meaningful source text (for example a hash), not just a prefix; two different line texts must invalidate the old ignore.
reproduction_steps: Open/import code with GetWorld()-> usage and no Engine/World.h on a line longer than 300 characters.
Ignore that built-in warning and save the project.
Regenerate or import a revised system preserving the line's first 300 characters but changing its ending expression.
The warning's truncated key still matches and it stays ignored.

findings.title: Valid methods after nested helper types are reported as undefined — class lookup ignores closing scopes
findings.surface: C++ tab compile check and Fix these issue input
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: in a UHealthComponent containing a plain nested FCache struct followed by UFUNCTION void Heal(), with UHealthComponent::Heal defined in the source, classAt returns FCache. The check reports 'UFUNCTION FCache::Heal ... never defined' and supplies this false issue to one-click Fix/export warnings. Developers must investigate/ignore the false diagnostic or risk approving an unnecessary AI repair. This is a deterministic source prediction, not an Unreal compile observation.
findings.evidence: compileCheck.js:110 records every class/struct opening, :111 returns the last opening preceding a UFUNCTION without tracking its closing brace, and :112 looks up that type's qualified definition. :130 emits a linker error when that mistaken qualified name is absent.
findings.expected: request: compile check links issues to 'the code that caused them'; checklist, Business logic and calculations: rules must use the correct object's identity. A method belongs to its enclosing class scope, not the nearest earlier type declaration, and an already defined valid method must not be labelled missing.
reproduction_steps: Import/open a header with UHealthComponent, a nested plain struct FCache { int Value; }; and then UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) void Heal();.
Include a corresponding UHealthComponent::Heal() definition in the source.
Open C++: the new classAt logic searches for FCache::Heal instead and emits a false missing-definition error.

findings.title: Keyboard focus escapes fix and bundle dialogs — the shared modal never isolates or focuses its active surface
findings.surface: Review the fix / Writing a fix / Bundle preset dialogs
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: after keyboard activation of Fix these or opening a preset, focus remains in the workspace and Tab can reach underlying buttons instead of staying in the dialog. Keyboard users can unknowingly open another project or invoke background actions during review; closing does not reliably return focus to the trigger. Pointer backdrop protection does not prevent keyboard interaction. No browser focus sequence was executed; the absence of enforcement is established in the shared primitive.
findings.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 only registers Escape; :11-18 adds a backdrop and aria-modal but no initial focus, focus trap, inert background or focus restoration. FixReviewModal.jsx:42 uses that primitive, passing null onClose while running. The trigger remains mounted behind the dialog.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: 'keyboard focus stays visible and follows the active surface' and dialogs preserve their focus/background interaction contract. The new review must allow keyboard users to reach Accept/Discard without interacting with the hidden workspace.
reproduction_steps: Use the keyboard to activate Fix these or a Bundle presets row.
Press Tab repeatedly while the dialog is open.
The code provides no focus move/trap, so background controls remain in the tab order and can be activated behind the overlay.

findings.title: Older saved presets become inaccessible after 200 — the list silently truncates with no next page
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: once a user saves 201 presets, the oldest is silently absent after refresh even though it remains stored. Users cannot open, rename or delete that preset from the product without removing newer entries until it surfaces. This is bounded library access loss, not proved database loss or measured performance degradation.
findings.evidence: projects.py:242 sorts presets newest first and calls to_list(200) with no pagination or total. PresetsList.jsx:9 assigns exactly r.data.presets, :30 renders only that array, and there is no page/load-more/search control in :25-40. No item GET route offers an alternate open path.
findings.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: 'Check pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation'; request: saved presets are reopened from the Bundle presets list. Saving a new preset must not silently make an existing one inaccessible.
reproduction_steps: Save 201 distinct bundle presets under the same account.
Reload the Projects panel.
Only the 200 most recently updated presets are returned/rendered; no older-page control or truncation notice exists.

findings.title: Presets forget selected projects that are not ready yet — Save stores only currently exportable ids
findings.surface: Bundle into one plugin > Save as preset
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: select Health, Stamina and Inventory where Inventory is readable but has no C++ yet. Because two valid modules remain, Save as preset succeeds but stores only Health/Stamina. When Inventory later acquires saved C++, reopening the preset still omits it forever; the user's chosen bundle intent was lost. They can recreate the preset manually, so this is recoverable.
findings.evidence: BundleModal.jsx:23 removes readable projects without both C++ files from valid; :29 sets loadedIds only from valid; :39 posts those loadedIds rather than the original selected ids. The no-C++ system is merely described as skipped at :26, with no indication that saving a preset permanently drops its selection.
findings.expected: R-247/request: Save as preset 'stores the plugin name and chosen projects'; presets later use 'their latest saved versions'. Export eligibility now must not silently change which project ids the saved preset remembers.
reproduction_steps: Select three projects, two with C++ and one with no C++ yet.
Open Bundle and Save as preset.
Later save C++ into the third project and reopen the preset.
Only the original two valid modules/ids were stored; the newly ready project is not selected.

findings.title: New stacked projects inherit another project's ignores — detaching the project leaves shared ignore state behind
findings.surface: Stack systems > new unsaved system > C++ check > Save project
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after ignoring a CoreMinimal.h warning in project A whose first line is #pragma once, stack two systems into a new unsaved system. If the generated header has that same warning/first line, it is already hidden by A's key; Save then persists A's ignore into the new project. Other teammates see a suppressed warning they never chose for this system. This is conditional on a matching diagnostic key in the new system, not an observed generation result.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:290 detaches a successfully stacked system with setProject(null), but never clears ignores. :545-548 still filters the new system against the preceding project's keys. On the next new-project save, :329 writes the retained ignores to the newly created project. setIgnores is otherwise called only on openProject (:370) and ignore actions (:562).
findings.expected: R-240: ignored keys are 'scoped to that project'; request: ignores are 'saved with the project'. A new stacked project must not inherit unrelated projects' warning decisions without an explicit choice.
reproduction_steps: In saved project A ignore 'CoreMinimal.h is not included.' on first line #pragma once.
Use Stack on two projects and obtain a new header with that same first line/missing-include warning.
Open C++ on the new unsaved stacked system; the old ignore remains active.
Save it as a new project: the old key is copied into its ignored_issues.

findings.title: Reviewing a small fix can exhaust browser resources on high-line-count files — unchanged files still run a quadratic full diff
findings.surface: Review the fix modal for accepted high-line-count .cpp input
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: a supported 60,000-character source containing 20,000 short '//\n' comment lines plus short code can approach 20,000 lines. Even a header-only fix computes the unchanged source's full ~400 million-cell LCS matrix: roughly 800 MB of typed-array storage plus overhead, synchronously in React render. This predicts severe browser resource pressure/unresponsiveness during review for that bounded input, not measured latency or a claim that typical projects freeze. Discard is not usable until rendering completes.
findings.evidence: FileDiff in FixReviewModal.jsx:8-9 calls sideBySideDiff before its equality return at :19, including for an unchanged .cpp. changes.js:49 allocates (n+1) Uint16Array(m+1) rows and :50-53 visits every cell. FixRequest accepts cpp_source up to 60000 characters (server.py:512).
findings.expected: checklist, Performance and resource leaks: 'Estimate work/resource growth ... material responsiveness ... loss'; the promised review must remain usable for accepted files, especially when only the other file changed.
reproduction_steps: Import a valid source near 60,000 characters with about 20,000 short comment/blank lines and a header with one repairable issue.
Run a fix that changes only the header, leaving cpp_source byte-identical.
When the reply arrives, FileDiff still allocates and computes the quadratic source diff before discovering that it is unchanged.

findings.title: Individual C++ downloads use filenames Unreal cannot resolve — download names come from the display title instead of generated.h
findings.surface: Workspace C++ tab and public-share C++ tab > individual .h/.cpp downloads
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: for a supported system_name='Health and Damage' whose header includes HealthAndDamageComponent.generated.h and whose source includes HealthAndDamageComponent.h, individual .h/.cpp buttons download Health_and_Damage.h/.cpp instead. A developer using these files must identify and repair the filenames before compiling; source zip export is an available alternative. This predicts an Unreal filename/include mismatch, not an executed compiler error.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:864-865 gives individual downloads the human system_name+'.h/.cpp'. CodeBox.jsx:29 sanitizes that title into the downloaded filename. zipExport.js:5-10 separately derives the authoritative base from the actual X.generated.h include, and :113-114 uses it for zip exports; the per-file path never calls that helper.
findings.expected: checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: delivered artifacts preserve the promised 'filename' and are usable in their intended format. Unreal's own include contract is explicit in the code: a header containing HealthAndDamageComponent.generated.h must be saved as HealthAndDamageComponent.h, not a human display title.
reproduction_steps: Open a system named Health and Damage with canonical HealthAndDamageComponent.generated.h in the header and HealthAndDamageComponent.h in its source include.
In C++, press the individual .h and .cpp download buttons.
The title-based filenames do not match the includes; compare with the canonical names used by Source files only zip export.

findings.title: Saved presets appear to disappear during a transient load failure — errors are converted into an empty hidden list
findings.surface: Projects > Bundle presets list on initial load or refresh failure
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: when a user with saved presets hits a transient server/network error during list refresh, the entire Bundle presets section disappears as if no presets exist, with no error or Retry. Stored data is not deleted, but users lose visible access and may recreate presets unnecessarily; reload or another successful refresh recovers them. This is a source-predicted dependency-failure state, not an observed outage.
findings.evidence: PresetsList.jsx:9 catches every GET /bundle-presets failure by setPresets([]), without a toast/error state or retention of the previous list. :25 then returns null for that array. Successful rename/delete calls load() at :16/:21, so this failure path also runs after an otherwise successful action.
findings.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: 'Resolve initial, empty, pending, success, failure ... states against the actual operation state' and provide visible feedback/recovery. A failed list request must not be presented as absence of the user's saved presets.
reproduction_steps: Load a Projects panel containing saved bundle presets.
Rename a preset, then let the subsequent GET /bundle-presets fail with a transient network/server error.
The code clears the list and removes its heading instead of showing failure and a retry action.

findings_minor.title: Developers cannot dismiss a pending fix — the running modal removes every close action
findings_minor.surface: Writing a fix… modal during a pending AI request
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: while the provider takes up to the 55-second server timeout, a developer who opened Fix accidentally cannot dismiss the blocking modal through X, Escape, backdrop or Discard. They must wait or reload; no code has yet changed. This is small, bounded interruption friction, not loss of saved work.
findings_minor.evidence: FixReviewModal.jsx:42 passes onClose=null while status==='running'. Modal.jsx:15 then omits the X button, :6 Escape calls no handler, and :11 backdrop has no active close callback. Running markup (:43-47) contains only a spinner/message and no cancel/close action.
findings_minor.expected: R-230 includes closing the modal before completion without changing code; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: interruption/recovery actions reach valid work for the same operation. Dismissing a pending proposal must not apply it.
reproduction_steps: Press Fix these and leave the provider request pending.
Try Escape, backdrop click or the normal close action.
All dialog dismissal paths are disabled/absent until the request finishes.

findings_minor.title: Editor API clients can save unsupported AI ignores that the UI cannot manage — ignore entries have no built-in-origin validation
findings_minor.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an Editor API client can submit an AI-review issue as an ignore and receive 200 with that entry persisted, although AI findings remain unsuppressed and the entry never appears in the UI's Ignored section for restoration. This is limited API-contract friction; the frontend correctly offers no AI Ignore button and no unauthorized suppression is established.
findings_minor.evidence: IgnoredIssue validates only lengths for arbitrary key/file/message (projects.py:124-128); set_ignores (:233-236) checks editor access but stores every supplied entry without checking built-in origin or correspondence to current diagnostics. Workspace.jsx:546-548 builds the visible ignored section only from keyed built-in check results, never from arbitrary stored entries.
findings_minor.expected: R-244: an AI finding 'cannot be added to PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores'; phase 1 request: 'Ignores apply to built-in check issues only'. Unsupported ignore entries should be refused rather than reported stored successfully.
reproduction_steps: As an Editor, obtain an AI-review finding.
Submit an ignore entry for it to PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores.
The handler accepts/stores it rather than rejecting unsupported AI ignores; reopen C++ and it is not a manageable built-in ignored issue.

findings_minor.title: API callers can save unusable one-project presets — project-count validation runs before id deduplication
findings_minor.surface: POST /api/bundle-presets; opening a malformed one-project preset
findings_minor.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an API caller submits two copies of one project id and receives a successfully saved preset containing only one distinct project. Reopening shows a bundle that cannot download. This is a minor validation/cleanup burden: the creator can delete the unusable preset and create a valid one. The normal checkbox UI deduplicates selections, so this is limited to direct/API clients.
findings_minor.evidence: PresetIn validates project_ids length 2–6 before normalization (projects.py:135-138). create_preset then deduplicates with list(dict.fromkeys(body.project_ids)) at :249 and inserts without revalidating. BundleModal.jsx:102-114 cannot download a resulting one-project preset.
findings_minor.expected: R-254: fewer than two projects must store no preset; request's bundle contract is 2–6 projects. Logical identity is project_id, so [A,A] contains one project, not two, independently of the array's raw length.
reproduction_steps: POST /api/bundle-presets with a valid plugin_name/name and the same readable project id twice.
Observe from the handler that the saved project_ids array is deduplicated to one item after validation.
Open that preset in the Projects panel; A bundle needs at least 2 projects with C++ is shown and Download is disabled.

findings_minor.title: AI issues with invalid negative line numbers jump outside the code — line validation omits the lower bound
findings_minor.surface: AI-review issue rows and their export-warning jump actions
findings_minor.observed: AI and model features: conditionally on an AI review returning line=-3 with a valid class/function in its message, clicking the issue targets a highlight above the code instead of that function or line 1. The developer must search manually. This is minor navigation friction; actual model output of this form was not executed.
findings_minor.evidence: server.py:488 accepts any int as an AI finding's line, including a negative one. locateIssue at compileCheck.js:170 treats a truthy negative integer as exact because it checks only line <= lines.length. CodeBox.jsx:50-51 then places the highlight at PAD_PX + (line-1)*LINE_PX, a negative position for line=-3, instead of using symbol fallback.
findings_minor.expected: R-211: issues without a usable exact line jump to 'the most likely class or function', or the file top. A source line position must satisfy 1 <= line <= number of source lines; invalid model coordinates must not bypass fallback.
reproduction_steps: Run AI review on code containing a named function.
Consider a reply with that function's diagnostic but line=-3.
Click the issue in the compile check or export warning: locateIssue returns the invalid line and never searches for the function.
